title: The performance plan
summary: Plan for nerves before they arrive: what a slip means, and exactly how the first ten seconds go.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: A bar of four beats: the first three silent, standing for walking up, sitting down and the one slow breath before playing, and the fourth played, the exact moment the piece begins.

steps.title: The performance plan
steps.body:
Nerves are not a problem to solve once and never feel again. They are a normal part of playing for people. The only real defence is a calm plan made in advance, before the nerves show up to make decisions for you.

1. Name what nerves actually feel like for you, in one honest sentence, said out loud.
2. Write the slip plan in words: keep the beat, carry on from the next bar, never stop to fix a mistake.
3. Plan the first ten seconds exactly: walk up, sit down, hands ready on the keys, one slow breath, begin.
4. Rehearse just those first ten seconds, five separate times this week, the exact same way every time.

The first ten seconds are the only part of a performance you can fully control before it starts. That is exactly why they are worth planning down to the breath.

figure.alt: The same bar, three silent beats then the piece begins, rehearsed five separate times this week the exact same way every time.

steps.title: Four sittings
steps.body: Fifteen minutes each. Tick a sitting when it is done. Days do not matter; sittings do.
checklist: Sitting 1: write the nerves sentence and the slip plan, say both out loud
Sitting 2: rehearse the first ten seconds three times
Sitting 3: rehearse the first ten seconds two more times, then play the piece
Sitting 4: the first ten seconds plus the whole piece, once as if recording
An old piece played once, using the same first ten seconds

steps.title: Record this week's version
steps.prompt: Record the first ten seconds exactly as planned, then play the piece once through, hands in the frame.
